svg.title: GANmapper: how a conditional GAN learns from paired maps
svg.desc: Road tile A enters the generator to make G(A). The same road tile is paired with the real building target B and with the generated image G(A). A PatchGAN discriminator compares the real and generated pairs and its feedback helps the generator improve. The local generated image is only a qualitative example. The conditional GAN topology follows Isola et al., CVPR 2017, Figure 2.
svg.text: GANmapper: how a conditional GAN learns from paired maps
The road tile is the condition. The generator proposes a building map; the discriminator compares generated and real pairs.
Generation: from the road tile to a proposed building map
D learns to distinguish the pairs; its judgment helps G improve the next proposal.
At inference: only the road tile and generator are needed. Compare the example output with the aligned target before judging quality.
